questions.question: You need to distinguish “aromatic compound” from several related chapter concepts. Which description uniquely identifies it?

options.label: A
options.text: A cyclic, planar, fully conjugated system with a qualifying number of pi electrons that receives unusual stabilization.

options.label: B
options.text: A five-membered aromatic heterocycle in which a nitrogen lone pair contributes to the aromatic pi system.

options.label: C
options.text: The six-membered aromatic hydrocarbon with delocalized pi electrons and equivalent carbon–carbon bonds.

options.label: D
options.text: A compound that fails one or more structural requirements for aromaticity and therefore is neither aromatic nor antiaromatic.

questions.correct_answer: A cyclic, planar, fully conjugated system with a qualifying number of pi electrons that receives unusual stabilization.
questions.explanation: The distinguishing description for aromatic compound is: A cyclic, planar, fully conjugated system with a qualifying number of pi electrons that receives unusual stabilization.
